examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931905/assets/e50848432dd18a4a5dc64d4e5a5cfb8b3e14e9fed6231774dd83ead5552cd463.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\dfrac{2\sqrt 6}{7},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $\csc\theta.$
examples.worked_solution:
Again, any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta$ as follows:

$$
x = \cos\theta, \qquad y = \sin\theta.
$$

We're given that $x=\dfrac{2\sqrt 6}{7}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\cos\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt 6}{7}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\sin\theta\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\cos\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt 6}{7}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{7})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{24}{49}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{25}{49}} \\  & =\pm \frac{5}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $\sin\theta$ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $\sin\theta = \dfrac{5}{7}.$

Finally, knowing that $\csc\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta},$ we have

$$
\csc\theta = \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{5}{7}\right)} = \dfrac{7}{5}.
$$

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{6}{7}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
cos⁡\theta =\frac{6}{7}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $sin⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $cos⁡\theta =\frac{6}{7}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{6}{7})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{36}{49}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{13}{49}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{13}}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we select the positive answer since $sin⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So our final answer is $sin⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{7}.$
